text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some simple best practices. First, give your endpoints clear names that describe the resources, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success and 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also important, because it helps other developers understand how to use your API. Finally, always think about versioning, so that old clients keep working when you make changes. A well-designed API is easy to read, easy to test, and easy to maintain over time.
